extracted.intended_audience: readers of literary criticism and history; students of religion, reform movements, and biography
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts evaluative principles for judging 'heroes', prophets, poets and reformers in history — what qualities mark a true hero or legitimate reform. Based on a literary-historical essay (biographical/critical treatment of Luther).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the Reformer vs Poet
rubrics_metrics.description: “The mild shining of the Poet's light has to give place to the fierce lightning of the Reformer ... The Poet indeed ... is the product and ultimate adjustment of Reform, or Prophecy, with its fierceness.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative distinction: poets represent a settled, perfected cultural moment while reformers are the violent agents who create new epochs. Use this to judge whether a figure functions as a conserver/celebrant of an age (poet) or as an active transformer (reformer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet as symptom of an epoch's completion
rubrics_metrics.description: “The finished Poet ... is a symptom that his epoch itself has reached perfection and is finished; that before long there will be a new epoch, new Reformers needed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A flourishing of polished poetic/artistic achievement can be read as evidence the cultural cycle is culminating; this signals likelihood of forthcoming reform. Interpret a 'finished' artist as an index of historical completion rather than purely individual greatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of forceful reform when obstructions accumulate
rubrics_metrics.description: “Obstructions are never wanting: the very things that were once indispensable furtherances become obstructions; and need to be shaken off, and left behind us,--a business often of enormous difficulty ... Offences accumulate till they become insupportable; and are then violently burst through, cleared off as by explosion.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for judging the legitimacy/need for reform: identify systemic practices that were once useful but now block progress. When such offences have accumulated, decisive, even violent, reform may be necessary. Example: Dante's Catholicism giving way to Luther's Protestantism; Feudalism to French Revolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity of belief as prerequisite for faithful action
rubrics_metrics.description: “A man who will _do_ faithfully, needs to believe firmly. If he have to ask at every turn the world's suffrage ... he is a poor eye-servant; the work committed to him will be _mis_done_.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess agents by whether their actions are grounded in firm, sincere conviction rather than performed for appearance or public approval. Anti-pattern: acting to please or to be seen, which leads to poor outcomes and contributes to systemic decay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insincere idolatry (Cant) is the principal evil
rubrics_metrics.description: “Condemnable Idolatry is _insincere_ Idolatry ... It is still a Thing Seen ... But here enters the fatal circumstance of Idolatry, that ... no man's mind _is_ any longer honestly filled with his Idol ... Condemnable Idolatry is _insincere_ Idolatry. Doubt has eaten out the heart of it ... It is equivalent to what we call Formulism, and Worship of Formulas.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between sincere symbolic practice and hypocritical/formulaic ritual. Prophetic critique is directed chiefly at insincere, formulaic worship ('cant'), which paralyzes moral life. In evaluating institutions or practices, ask whether participants genuinely hold the beliefs or merely perform their signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: All worship proceeds by symbols; idolatry is comparative
rubrics_metrics.description: “Idol is _Eidolon_, a thing seen, a symbol. ... All creeds, liturgies, religious forms, conceptions that fitly invest religious feelings, are in this sense _eidola_, things seen. All worship whatsoever must proceed by Symbols, by Idols:--we may say, all Idolatry is comparative, and the worst Idolatry is only _more_ idolatrous.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating religious or symbolic systems, recognize that symbolic mediation is inevitable; the critique should focus on degree and sincerity, not on mere use of symbols. Use comparative judgment rather than absolute condemnation of symbol-use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophet/Hero as 'Idol-breaker' who returns people to reality
rubrics_metrics.description: “I find Luther to have been a Breaker of Idols ... It is the property of every Hero, in every time, in every place and situation, that he come back to reality; that he stand upon things, and not shows of things.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key test of a genuine reforming hero: readiness to expose and dismantle false shows, institutions, or practices and to re-ground life in perceived realities. Examples: Luther denouncing indulgences and burning the papal bull. Evaluate figures by whether they prioritize substantive truth over appearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private judgment, when sincere, unites rather than fragments
rubrics_metrics.description: “The exercise of private judgment, faithfully gone about, does by no means necessarily end in selfish independence, isolation; but rather ends necessarily in the opposite of that. It is not honest inquiry that makes anarchy; but it is error, insincerity, half-belief and untruth that make it.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the social effects of 'private judgment' by the sincerity of its practitioners. Honest, conscientious private judgment tends toward communion with others who seek truth; half-belief breeds anarchy. Do not equate private judgment automatically with social fragmentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality is sincerity, not mere novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: “The merit of _originality_ is not novelty; it is sincerity. The believing man is the original man; whatsoever he believes, he believes it for himself, not for another.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing creative or intellectual originality, prioritize authenticity of conviction over mere newness. A work or belief is 'original' if genuinely appropriated and sincerely held, even if derived from predecessors.

rubrics_metrics.name: True Hero = sincere man; hero-worship grounded on realities
rubrics_metrics.description: “Hero-worship never dies, nor can die. Hero mean _sincere man_ ... Loyalty and Sovereignty are everlasting in the world:--and there is this in them, that they are grounded not on garnitures and semblances, but on realities and sincerities.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for honoring persons: base reverence on their genuine moral/spiritual reality, not on pomp or outward trappings. Evaluate leaders by underlying sincerity and concrete service rather than ceremonial authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origins and hardship as qualifications for reforming disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is altogether suitable to Luther's function ... that he was born poor, and brought up poor ... Hardship, rigorous Necessity was the poor boy's companion; ... Among things, not among the shows of things, had he to grow.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider formative biography (poverty, hardship, early exposure to 'realities') as relevant to a person's capacity to critique and reform entrenched falsehoods. Such background may cultivate practical seriousness and resistance to mere appearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conscience and appeal to scripture/plain argument as standard of truthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: At the Diet of Worms: “Confute me by proofs of Scripture, or else by plain just arguments: I cannot recant otherwise. For it is neither safe nor prudent to do aught against conscience. Here stand I; I can do no other: God assist me!”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate truth-claims and moral stands by their openness to reasoned argument and authoritative texts (in that context, Scripture) and by the actor's adherence to conscience. A legitimate stance invites rational refutation rather than blind coercion; refusal to recant without such refutation evidences principled moral integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to face personal danger and notoriety for truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Luther 'would not be advised' against appearing at Worms despite warnings; he burned the papal Bull and accepted the consequences when challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging the authenticity of a reformer or prophet, note readiness to accept personal risk, public censure, or even violence rather than compromise truth. Courage under threat is evidence of sincerity and conviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of progress-talk; focus on concrete enlargement of view
rubrics_metrics.description: “I do not make much of 'Progress of the Species' ... The fact itself seems certain enough ... Every man ... is not only a learner but a doer: he learns ... but with the same mind he discovers farther, he invents and devises somewhat of his own. Absolutely without originality there is no man.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague or extravagant talk about abstract 'progress'; evaluate change in terms of concrete enlargements of understanding and fresh discoveries that alter credible belief. Emphasize empirical/experiential enlargement over rhetorical claims of teleological progress.
